# Check flux on the field you actually represent

[Integrate the Fourier interpolant, then ask what a nodal quadrature adds.]{.lesson-deck}
:::

A divergence-free periodic velocity should have zero net outward flux
through a closed rectangle. The retained flow diagnostic checks that
statement for the represented trigonometric field. Its helper named
`face_flux` integrates Fourier modes; it is distinct from OpenPFC's
finite-volume face-field operators.

For $B=[x_0,x_1]\times[y_0,y_1]$, write the outward flux as

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Phi_x&=\int_{y_0}^{y_1}\!\bigl[u(x_1,y)-u(x_0,y)\bigr]dy,\\
\Phi_y&=\int_{x_0}^{x_1}\!\bigl[v(x,y_1)-v(x,y_0)\bigr]dx,\\
\Phi&=\Phi_x+\Phi_y.
\end{aligned}
$$

The signs come from the outward normal: right and top are positive,
left and bottom negative. Integrating the represented divergence gives
the same flux, up to floating point effects when evaluating the sums.

## Integrate each mode analytically

A mode separates into exponentials along the two axes. Its one-dimensional
integral has a removable zero-wavenumber case:

$$
\int_a^b e^{iks}ds=
\begin{cases}
b-a,&k=0,\\
(e^{ikb}-e^{ika})/(ik),&k\ne0.
\end{cases}
$$

```{.cpp include="../ns2d/flux_balance.hpp" snippet="integrate_mode"}
```

The helper sums those integrals over normalized velocity coefficients.
The forward transform is unscaled, so it divides by the global cell count
before interpreting a coefficient as a physical amplitude.

A real-to-complex spectrum stores only nonnegative $k_x$. For interior
stored $k_x$, the helper also adds the conjugate mode at $(-k_x,-k_y)$.
It avoids adding that partner twice on the zero and Nyquist planes, whose
partners are already represented. The retained flow states have zero
Nyquist coefficients under the two-thirds mask. A small imaginary remainder is a useful
check of this reconstruction.

## Test more than the full period

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="boxes"}
```

The boxes include the whole domain, smaller aligned rectangles, one cell
and an off-node rectangle. The analytic mode integrals work at arbitrary
box coordinates; the corners need not be grid nodes.

The full-period integral of divergence is zero for **every** periodic
Fourier velocity, because its derivative has zero DC. That single number
therefore cannot establish incompressibility. Smaller boxes and nonzero
modal divergence coefficients ask a stronger question.

The diagnostic also computes the largest normalized modal amplitude of
$ik_x\widehat u+ik_y\widehat v$, using the same odd derivative symbols as
the solver. Interpret that alongside the nodal divergence norms and the
individual box fluxes.

## Keep the quadrature comparison separate

The `trap_net` column applies composite trapezoidal quadrature to the
nodal velocity on aligned box faces. It samples the same field through a
different numerical operation. On a subinterval, that quadrature can have
error even when the Fourier interpolant is divergence free.

When a corner is off-node, the helper returns no trapezoid value and the
CSV cell is empty. Treat that as unavailable data, rather than zero flux.
`relative` divides the signed net flux by the sum of absolute face
integrals; when that denominator vanishes, the program records zero.
Inspect the absolute `net` column and the scale as well.

## Run the retained diagnostic

From the repository root, with a compatible installed spectral CPU SDK:

```sh
mkdir -p results
openpfc compile examples/flow/flux-balance/model.cpp --source-root examples/flow -o results/flux-balance
results/flux-balance --case two-mode --n 16 --dt 0.02 --times 0.02 --nu 0.05 --outdir results/flow/flux-balance
```

Use one MPI rank, as required by this driver so its mode sum owns every
coefficient. This small case retains the existing CTest smoke settings.
The executable name remains `ns2d_flux_balance` at its original build
location. The [model](model.cpp) shares
[flux_balance.hpp](../ns2d/flux_balance.hpp),
[cases.hpp](../ns2d/cases.hpp),
[vorticity_stream.hpp](../ns2d/vorticity_stream.hpp) and
[spectral.hpp](../ns2d/spectral.hpp); keep that relative layout when
using downloads.

Read `flux_balance.csv` and `run.json`. Compare `net`, `imag`, `trap_net`,
`modal_div`, `div_linf` and `div_l2` across the different boxes. `status`
reports the run's finite-field and CFL guards; it does not apply a flux
accuracy threshold. The retained numerical tests exercise the integration
helpers separately.

Repeat at a finer grid and at a later, common physical time. A change in
nodal trapezoid error is a quadrature question. A change in the underlying
velocity after grid or time refinement is a solution-accuracy question.
Keeping them separate makes a conservation diagnostic useful.
